Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the StellarTech Solutions Q1 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today's call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Emily Carter, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter, VP of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and welcome to StellarTech Solutions’ Q1 earnings call. Joining me today are Robert Thompson, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; and David Lee, Chief Technology Officer.
Earlier today, we published our earnings press release and presentation, which are available on our Investor Relations site. Today’s discussion may include forward-looking statements. With that, let me turn the call over to Robert.

Robert Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Emily, and welcome everyone.

We’re pleased with our performance this quarter. I want to highlight a few areas:

First, I'd like to address our foundry customer outlook and design win momentum. During the first half of 2020, specifically in Q2, we experienced a significant surge in 28nm design activity at UMC. This upswing was driven by increased customer tape-outs, reflecting our strategic positioning in addressing the growing demand for cost-effective, power-efficient solutions in sectors like display drivers, IoT connectivity, and entry-level smartphones. We saw a 45% increase in the number of unique 28nm designs taped out in H1 2020 compared to H2 2019. Q2 2020 showed a pronounced surge, with tape-out volumes exceeding those of Q1 2020 by 28%. The transition to higher resolution displays in entry-level and mid-range smartphones fueled demand for 28nm DDICs. UMC's 28HPC+ process, optimized for display applications, proved particularly attractive to customers. We saw a 60% increase in tape-outs for display driver applications compared to the previous half. Key design wins included partnerships with three major Taiwanese DDIC manufacturers, resulting in an estimated $45 million in potential revenue over the next 12 months. Our 28nm Low Power (LP) process has garnered significant traction, with notable design wins in Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) and Wi-Fi chipsets. We secured a major design win with a leading European IoT connectivity provider, projecting $20 million in revenue over the product lifecycle. We witnessed increased activity from Chinese fabless companies designing application processors (APs) and baseband solutions on UMC's 28nm platform. Designs for automotive display controllers and sensor interfaces are contributing to the overall 28nm volume. Taiwanese fabless companies continue to be the primary drivers of 28nm demand, accounting for approximately 65% of the tape-outs in H1 2020. We observed a significant increase in design activity from Chinese customers, representing around 25% of the total tape-outs. The remaining 10% of tape-outs originated from customers in North America, Europe, and other Asian countries. We continued to enhance our 28HPC+ process, focusing on improved power efficiency and performance, and introduced a new low-leakage transistor option, resulting in a 10% reduction in standby power consumption for certain designs. We are actively working on integrating embedded flash memory into our 28nm process, targeting applications requiring secure storage and fast read/write speeds. We expect to have initial samples available to customers by the end of Q3 2020. The increased 28nm tape-out activity is expected to translate into higher revenue in the second half of 2020 and beyond. We project a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion, driven in part by the ramp-up of 28nm production.

Our Q2 capacity expansion is strategically focused on meeting the anticipated surge in demand for advanced node semiconductors, particularly those supporting the burgeoning AI and high-performance computing (HPC) markets. The primary driver of capacity growth this quarter is the ramp-up of fab8N, complemented by a smaller, but crucial, capacity increase within fab12A. This expansion is projected to contribute to a 12% increase in overall wafer output compared to Q1. Our advanced node manufacturing facility, fab8N, is primarily dedicated to producing chips using a 7nm and 5nm process. We are implementing a phased capacity expansion within fab8N, involving the installation of 32 additional EUV (Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography) machines. We project a 25% increase in wafer starts by the end of Q2 at Fab8N, bringing its total capacity to approximately 85,000 wafers per month, a significant step towards our target of 110,000 wafers per month by the end of the year. We've allocated $750 million for equipment purchases, infrastructure upgrades, and personnel training related to this expansion in Q2. The incremental increase in fab12A focuses on optimizing existing production lines and improving process efficiency. We are projecting a 5% increase in wafer starts at Fab12A through these improvements, bringing its total capacity to approximately 145,000 wafers per month. The fab12A improvements are less capital intensive, with an estimated $150 million allocated for upgrades in Q2. To further enhance the performance of our advanced node chips, we are investing in advanced packaging technologies, such as 2.5D and 3D stacking. We are also investing in research and development related to new materials and process technologies. We are implementing AI-driven manufacturing solutions to optimize our production processes, improve yield rates, and reduce equipment downtime.

Finally, looking at our Q2 2020 guidance, we anticipate a solid quarter, driven by incremental improvements in both wafer shipments and average selling prices (ASPs). While we are not expecting a dramatic surge, the combination of these factors, coupled with continued cost optimization efforts, should allow us to maintain a healthy gross margin of approximately 20%. Based on current forecasts, we project Q2 2020 revenue to be in the range of $1.85 billion to $1.89 billion. We are projecting a 1% to 2% increase in wafer shipments compared to Q1 2020. Our ASP in U.S. dollars is expected to increase by 1% to 2% in Q2 2020. We anticipate a gross profit margin of approximately 20% for Q2 2020. We are continuing to focus on cost optimization initiatives across our manufacturing operations. We have implemented several initiatives to improve wafer yields in our fabs, which is helping to reduce scrap and rework costs. The slight decrease in gross margin compared to Q1 is partially attributable to the costs associated with ramping up production of our new 7nm chips in our Fab 1 (U.S.) facility. Existing tariffs and trade restrictions continue to present a challenge, contributing to slightly higher COGS.

I’ll now pass it over to Sarah to walk through the numbers in more detail.

Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Robert, and hello, everyone.

Let me break it down starting with our P&L guidance for Q2 2020. To reiterate Robert's points, we are projecting revenue to be between $1.85 billion and $1.89 billion, representing a 2.5% to 4.7% increase compared to the previous quarter. We saw healthy growth driven by our key customers in the automotive and industrial sectors, specifically in our advanced power management ICs for electric vehicles and sensors used in industrial automation. We are aiming for a gross margin of approximately 20%, navigating the challenges of ramping up 7nm production and mitigating the impact of tariffs through strategic sourcing and supply chain diversification.

Now, moving to our wafer sales for this quarter, which we’ve been tracking closely. This quarter's wafer shipments reached NT$2.15 million, measured in 8-inch equivalent wafers. Our actual shipments comprise a mix of wafer sizes. Estimated shipment volume of 8-inch Wafers is 1.3 million wafers. Estimated shipment volume of 12-inch Wafers is 600,000 wafers. Converted to 8-inch equivalents, this is roughly 1.35 million wafers. Estimated shipment volume of 6-inch & Smaller Wafers is 200,000 wafers. Converted to 8-inch equivalents, this is roughly 0.1 million wafers. Total Estimated Equivalent 8-inch Wafer Shipments is 2.75 million wafers. ASP averaged NT$450 per 8-inch wafer, a slight 2% decrease compared to the previous quarter. ASP averaged NT$850 per 12-inch wafer, a 5% increase compared to the previous quarter. ASP averaged NT$100 per 6-inch & Smaller Wafers. 8-inch Wafers revenue is NT$585 million, 12-inch Wafers revenue is NT$510 million, 6-inch & Smaller Wafers revenue is NT$20 million, with Total Estimated Revenue (Wafer Sales) at NT$1.115 billion. We saw strong demand for 12-inch wafers in North America, steady demand for both 8-inch and 12-inch wafers in Asia-Pacific, moderate growth in China, and stable demand across all wafer sizes in Europe. We are continuing to invest in expanding our 12-inch wafer capacity and are increasingly focusing on integrating wafer manufacturing with advanced packaging solutions. Our yield improvement programs have reduced the wafer scrap rate by 2% QoQ.

Lastly, I'd like to briefly touch on our sales by segment. Communication remained at 54% of the pie which is the largest share of our application breakdown. Communication generated $2.7 billion in revenue this quarter, a 15% increase YoY. This growth was driven by increased adoption of our unified communication platform among enterprise clients and strong performance within our embedded communication solutions for the healthcare sector. Our cloud-based platform, "ConnectSphere," accounted for 65% of the segment's revenue. The Communication segment achieved a gross margin of 68% this quarter, a slight increase of 1% compared to Q3 2023. North America remains our strongest region for the Communication segment, contributing approximately 45% of the segment's revenue. A significant trend within the communication segment is the increasing demand for AI-powered features. Our Collaboration Segment grew by a robust 22% YoY with revenue at $1.1 billion and a margin of 72%. Our Security segment revenue reached $700 million, a 28% YoY increase with a margin of 65%. Our Analytics segment revenue reached $500 million, a 12% increase YoY with a margin of 60%.

Now, let me hand things over to David to talk about product and operational progress.

David Lee, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, Sarah.

This was a busy quarter for our teams. On the innovation front, we made meaningful advances around AI integration across all our product lines. This included the release of ClarityAI, which is already gaining traction in the contact center space by providing real-time sentiment analysis during customer interactions.

Also worth noting is our improvement in our foundry customer relationships. Our focus on process optimization, customer collaboration, and strategic partnerships has enabled us to capitalize on the growing demand for cost-effective, power-efficient solutions, especially in the 28nm space. We believe we are gaining ground against our competitors in this segment.

And we’ve made foundational changes in how we approach capacity expansion, particularly on the fulfillment and logistics side. We are working closely with our equipment suppliers to secure timely delivery of the new EUV machines for fab8N, diversifying our sourcing to minimize disruptions, and investing in training and development programs to build a pipeline of talent.

Let’s now open the floor for questions.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
Hi, thanks for taking my question. On sales by segment, could you expand on what’s driving that strength in the collaboration segment?

Robert Thompson:
Certainly. The collaboration segment's growth is significantly bolstered by the launch of our integrated project planning suite, "ProjectZenith", which has seen strong adoption in the construction and engineering sectors. The margin in this segment is high, benefiting from software sales. We anticipate that the collaboration segment will continue to grow rapidly in the next few quarters, and we are exploring strategic acquisitions to further strengthen our position in this market.

Analyst 2:
A follow-up on wafer sales. How confident are you that you can maintain the ASP for 12-inch wafers, given the increasing competition?

Sarah Chen:
We are confident in our ability to maintain a healthy ASP for 12-inch wafers through several strategies. First, we are focused on a product mix shift towards higher-margin applications like AI accelerators and high-performance computing. Second, we are integrating wafer manufacturing with advanced packaging solutions to offer more comprehensive and higher-value solutions. Finally, our ongoing yield improvement programs and AI-driven process control systems are helping to reduce defect density and increase overall efficiency, which supports our pricing power.

Analyst 3:
And for AI integration, any update on the development of AI-driven manufacturing solutions?

David Lee:
Yes, we're making excellent progress. We are implementing AI-driven manufacturing solutions to optimize our production processes, improve yield rates, and reduce equipment downtime. This includes using machine learning algorithms to predict equipment failures, optimize process parameters, and identify potential bottlenecks. The latest implementation of AI-driven process control systems has already shown a 3% reduction in defect density on the 12-inch line.

Analyst 4:
Just a final one — on capacity expansion, is the improvement mostly driven by the addition of new equipment, or are there other factors at play?

Sarah Chen:
While the addition of new equipment, particularly the EUV machines in fab8N, is a significant driver, it's not the only factor. We are also focusing on optimizing existing production lines, improving process efficiency, and implementing advanced process control (APC) systems in fab12A. These improvements, while less capital intensive, contribute significantly to the overall capacity increase and improve our operational efficiency. Additionally, we are investing in training and development programs to ensure we have the skilled workforce needed to operate the new and existing equipment effectively.

Closing

Robert Thompson:
Thank you again for joining us today. We remain confident in our long-term growth story and are committed to disciplined execution. We appreciate your continued interest and support.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes today’s call. You may now disconnect.
